Course · Whole course on one page

The Queen and the hive: how the t27 project builds itself

This project builds itself: an issue becomes a task for a bee, the bee writes a t27 spec, a reviewer bee checks it, it merges, and the site regenerates. The Queen who runs that loop is written as t27 specs with tests, and every widget here runs the fn bodies of one of them compiled to WebAssembly.

Course 11, 27 lessons, a live widget and a t27 spec each: shaping an issue, priority and review first, a task's life, the reviewer and the merge gate, the review jam, keys, credit and tokens, agents in one group, the night watch and the board. Every answer comes from a compiled spec.

Every course is free, for everyone: no sign-up, no email, nothing to pay.

01

Module 1 · The task

An issue becomes work only once it is shaped: the sections it lacks are written or asked for, its boundary names real files, and one filter reads every kind of task.

01

Lesson 1 of 27

Shaping an issue

You will learnWhat the Queen does with an issue that lacks sections, and why she stops after two tries.

A bee can start only on an issue that says what to do and which files it may touch. The Queen holds every open issue to judge() of specs/policy/issue_shape.t27. One that is not ready she shapes: a model writes the missing sections, and the body goes back only if judge() then finds nothing missing. After SHAPE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT, 2 failed shapes, she stops and comments once with what is missing, and an epic is never shaped. shape_action in shaping.t27 decides, and a new try waits 360 minutes.

Try it

Set two sections missing and step through the tries; then mark the author told and see which column the issue goes to.

Open the interactive lesson →
02

Lesson 2 of 27

A boundary of real files

You will learnWhich proposed paths a task may reserve, and why one invented path stops the whole shape.

A task's boundary is a reservation: while a bee works, no other bee takes those files. So a wrong boundary is worse than a missing one, because it holds files the work does not own. path_accepted takes any file that exists, and a new file only when its folder exists, the issue cites it, and its language is one the only-t27 rule allows. shape_lands writes the shape back only when no section is missing, it names 1 to 12 paths, and none of them was refused.

Try it

Make the two red paths green by changing only facts that could be true; then leave a section missing and watch the gate.

Open the interactive lesson →
03

Lesson 3 of 27

One task, three kinds

You will learnHow an issue, a review and a job become one kind of task with seven states, and how one filter reads them.

The Queen runs three kinds of work: issues for bees, reviews of finished work, and jobs. Each kept its own codes, so no board could show them together. tasks.t27 gives them 7 shared states, numbered as the board's columns plus failed. A cancelled job shows as dropped, and so does a review row that was forgotten. task_matches is the filter the board, the game and the route all apply: a bit per kind, a bit per state, and 0 means any.

Try it

Show only failed tasks of every kind; then find which job state shows as dropped.

02

Module 2 · Who goes next

The order the Queen takes issues in: a label ages one step, at most 3 criticals run as critical, and nothing new starts while finished work waits for review.

04

Lesson 4 of 27

Aging a label

You will learnHow a labelled issue moves up with age, and why only by one level.

Without labels the Queen takes issues in GitHub's listing order. priority.t27 adds four levels, critical, high, normal and low; lower runs first, and an unlabelled issue counts as normal. A labelled issue gains one level after AGING_DAYS, 14 days, and at most MAX_AGING_STEPS, 1 level, so a low issue reaches normal on day 14 and stays there. High and critical do not age. effective_level computes the line the widget draws.

Try it

Find the day a labelled low issue moves up; then remove the label and drag to day 60.

Open the interactive lesson →
05

Lesson 5 of 27

The queue

You will learnHow the cap, aging and blockers order a queue of open issues.

Labels inflate: if every issue is critical, none is. capped_level lets at most CRITICAL_CAP, 3, issues of a listing run as critical, taken in listing order, and the 4th runs as high. An issue with an open blocker is skipped, not waited on, so it cannot hold up the queue. outranks compares the effective level, then the real level, then the place in the listing, so an aged issue never beats a real one of its level. why names the reason for each place.

Try it

Make a fifth issue critical and see where it lands; then label the unlabelled issue low.

Open the interactive lesson →
06

Lesson 6 of 27

Review first

You will learnWhy the Queen closes the backlog while finished work waits for a review, and what still goes.

On 2026-10-18 the status page read 69 of 70 workers busy, and in one hour 102 dispatches, 56 finished and 11 reviewed. Bees started about nine for every verdict, and each new bee held files that the bees in review needed when they were sent back. review_first.t27 closes the backlog while the review queue is longer than REVIEW_QUEUE_MAX, 0. Work the review sent back and work the owner assigned still go: admission admits them at any queue length.

Try it

Drag the queue to 0 and back to 1; then find the candidates that are admitted at any length.

03

Module 3 · A bee's life

From candidate to done: twelve states and sixteen events, a ship in the game that flies home, and a deploy that does not cut a bee short.

07

Lesson 7 of 27

A task's life

You will learnWhich states a dispatched task passes through, and which events are legal in each.

dispatch.t27 is the Queen's task lifecycle, the cycle that chooses, starts, ends, reviews and releases work. A task has 12 states and 16 events. next_state answers every pair, and 99 means the event is illegal in that state: a verdict cannot reach a running task, and a reap cannot reach an ended one. After a verdict a send-back waits for its floor and is released; even an accept is sent back if CI turns red under the ceiling.

Try it

Walk a task from none to accept; then make CI red at the ceiling and find the one way out.

Open the interactive lesson →
08

Lesson 8 of 27

The ship flies home

You will learnWhere the game draws a bee for each thing it is doing, and how a finished task ends on screen.

In the game at app.t27.ai/game each bee is a ship over the issue it works on. ship_mode in hive.t27 picks the place: parked at the entrance before a runner claims it, orbiting its cell while it is heard from, hovering when it has gone quiet, and waiting at its repository's portal until its cell is placed. When the bee leaves the feed it flies home, and ship_alpha fades it over DEPART_MS, 2400 ms: at 1200 ms it is at 500 of 1000.

Try it

Mark the bee as not heard from and see where it moves; then drag the time past 2400 ms.

Open the interactive lesson →
09

Lesson 9 of 27

A deploy mid-flight

You will learnWhat a redeploy does to a bee, a review, a round, a job and a wait.

Every merge redeploys the Queen, and work is running when it does. drain.t27 sorts that work. A round, a job step and a wait row are rows the store keeps: the process leaves them and the next process carries on. A review is stopped, because a stop loses at most one review, which is redone. A bee is held, because what it has done lives in its conversation; at the cap, drain_cap_seconds, 1800 s today, it is handed back and its work is salvaged into its branch.

Try it

Drag the wait from 0 to the cap and watch the bee's row change; then cut the platform drain to 1000 s.

Open the interactive lesson →
04

Module 4 · The reviewer bee

Finished work is judged on its own clock: enough reviews at once to keep up, a pause that doubles for a row that waits, and a merge gate that zero checks cannot open.

10

Lesson 10 of 27

Enough reviewers

You will learnHow many reviews must run at once for the reviewer to keep up with the bees.

A review may take REVIEW_ROW_SECONDS, 300 s, so one slot clears at most 12 rows an hour. On 2026-10-09 bees finished about 58 an hour while 111 rows waited, and the fixed REVIEWER_CONCURRENCY of 4 tops out at 48. slots_needed(58) is 5. reviewer_concurrency takes the keys, their lanes and the free memory, never goes above 16 and never below 1 while anything waits, and keeps_up compares it with the finish rate.

Try it

Find the fewest keys of 1 lane that keep up with 58 an hour; then cut the memory to 1000 MB.

Open the interactive lesson →
11

Lesson 11 of 27

Back off

You will learnWhy a row that answers wait is visited less and less often, and how often at least.

Over 44 minutes on 2026-10-09 the reviewer made 941 row visits, 888 of them wait, from 22 rows whose branch it could not read; one row was visited 54 times. revisit_after_seconds now waits 30 s after one wait and doubles per wait, never past 900 s: 30, 60, 120, 240, 480, 900. due_again lets the row be taken only once that time has passed, and any other answer resets the count.

Try it

Find the wait count where the pause stops growing; then set 4 waits and find the second the row is due.

Open the interactive lesson →
12

Lesson 12 of 27

The merge gate

You will learnWhen the merger may merge a pull request a reviewer bee approved.

The reviewer bee approves, and the merger merges; merger_gate.t27 is the rule between them. check_passes lets a green check through and blocks any check still running. A red one passes only when it is not required, has concluded, and the bee named it as discounted, and with the ruleset unreadable every check counts as required. gate_open needs at least 1 posted check, 0 running and 0 blocking: zero checks is not zero failures.

Try it

Let the running check conclude green; then make the ruleset unreadable and watch the discounted red.

Open the interactive lesson →
05

Module 5 · The review jam

A pull request that will not move is in exactly one of ten cases, each with the Queen's move, and a red check is inherited only when master says so.

13

Lesson 13 of 27

The review jam

You will learnWhich of ten cases a stuck pull request is in, and why the earliest matching rule wins.

A pull request can stall for many reasons at once: refused, pushed again, and red on a noise check. review-jam.t27 gives the Queen one answer. jam_case checks 9 facts in a fixed order and the earliest rule that matches wins, so a PR the Queen could not measure is never reported as free, and one that was refused and then pushed is not taken for noise. There are 10 cases, from none to unmeasured.

Try it

Clear facts one by one from the start state and name each case you pass; then find a PR that is in no jam.

Open the interactive lesson →
14

Lesson 14 of 27

The Queen's move

You will learnWhat the Queen does for each jam, and which jams she waits on.

Each case has one action at the same position: no reviewer dispatches a reviewer, refused not fixed dispatches the coder, refused then pushed dispatches a re-review, and labeled not merged finishes the merge. jam_action maps any value above 9 to measure again, so an unknown case is never nothing to do. jam_is_queens_turn is false for 3 cases, none, draft or fresh, and stacked on an open PR: she waits on those.

Try it

Find the case whose action is wait for the base; then drag to 200 and read the action.

Open the interactive lesson →
15

Lesson 15 of 27

Inherited red

You will learnWhen a red check on a pull request is inherited from master, and why a cancelled run says nothing.

A bee may approve a PR with a red check when that check is red on master too. On 2026-10-06 a PR merged red because master's run of that check was cancelled and was read as red. Now the merger reads master itself, newest run first: run_says counts only a completed failure or success, look_back passes over everything else and over runs older than the merge base, and discount_holds needs the bee's word and MASTER RED.

Try it

Make every run cancelled; then move the failure before the merge base and look at the gate.

Open the interactive lesson →
06

Module 6 · Keys

A bee's model key can be refused: the code in the body sorts the refusal, a transient one rests the key for seconds, and the bee moves on to the next free key.

16

Lesson 16 of 27

A refused key

You will learnHow the Queen sorts a provider's refusal into transient, quota, auth or a bad request.

Bees call models with keys, and keys get refused. key_failover.t27 sorts each refusal with error_kind. The z.ai code in the body wins over the HTTP status, because z.ai sends a spent quota and a passing overload with the same 429: code 1305 is transient, 1113 is quota. No answer at all is transient. A quota or auth refusal closes the key, and only a bad request is charged to the issue.

Try it

Compare 429 with codes 1308 and 1312; then read what no answer at all is.

Open the interactive lesson →
17

Lesson 17 of 27

A key rests

You will learnHow long a refused key rests before a bee may use it again.

A transient refusal rests the key COOL_BASE_SECONDS, 15 s, doubled per strike in a row and never more than COOL_CAP_SECONDS, 240 s: 15, 30, 60, 120, 240. A spent quota or a refused key closes it for KEY_BREAK_SECONDS, 1800 s. cooldown_seconds gives all of it. The rest is short so that 34 keys are never all resting through a one-minute burst like the one of 2026-10-17.

Try it

Find the strike count where the rest stops growing; then switch to quota and read the rest.

Open the interactive lesson →
18

Lesson 18 of 27

The next key

You will learnWhich key a bee tries next, and when it moves to another pool or gives up.

On 2026-10-17 a bee started on key 9 of 10 and died 7 s later while 33 other keys stood by: it got one key at dispatch and kept it. next_free now picks the next key after the last one that is neither tried nor resting. 1305 is an overload of the pool's model, so once POOL_OVERLOAD_KEYS, 3, keys said it within a minute, step moves the bee to the next pool. After 8 attempts the turn ends.

Try it

Mark key 2 as tried and see which key gets the ring; then set three keys that said 1305.

07

Module 7 · Credit and money

Lending a key earns no credit, an operation is sold at twice its cost in half-cent tokens, and tokens burn 30 days after they land.

19

Lesson 19 of 27

No credit for keys

You will learnWhat a contributor's lent keys earn, and which limits keep them safe.

Anyone can lend the hive model keys through queen-contributor-keys.t27. A key is probed before it is enabled: at most 4 probes at once, a new probe waits out 60 s after the last, and an owner holds at most 100 keys. Lending earns nothing by itself: CREDIT_WALLET is false, so wallet_credit answers 0 for any number of keys. XP follows the work the Queen records.

Try it

Drag the keys from 0 to 100 and watch the credit meter; then find the second a probe may start.

Open the interactive lesson →
20

Lesson 20 of 27

Twice the cost

You will learnHow the project prices an operation and what a month of tokens buys.

Every dollar becomes tokens at one rate, TOKEN_MICRO_USD 5000: a token is half a cent. price_tokens sells an operation at twice what it costs, MARKUP_PCT 200, and rounds up so nothing sells below that: a cost of 12300 micro-dollars is 5 tokens. month_tokens turns $20 into 4000 tokens, which is 14 reels of 270 tokens or 333 portraits of 12.

Try it

Find the costs that give exactly 1 token; then find the monthly price that buys 36 reels.

Open the interactive lesson →
21

Lesson 21 of 27

Tokens that burn

You will learnWhen a batch of tokens burns, and which batch is spent first.

The owner's rule of 2026-10-01: all money goes into tokens, and tokens not spent within the month burn, so a person who paid makes content instead of saving tokens. Each batch lives MONTH_DAYS, 30 days, and days_left counts it down from the day it landed. On day 25 the package month from day 0 has 5 days left, the start gift from day 3 has 8, and a top-up from day 12 has 17. The spend order is soonest burn first.

Try it

Find the day the package month burns; then find the last day any batch is left.

Open the interactive lesson →
08

Module 8 · Agents among themselves

One bot per agent in one group: who is called, a chain three bot messages deep, and the clocks that keep agents from flooding a chat.

22

Lesson 22 of 27

Who is called

You will learnWhich messages in the hive group wake an agent, from a person and from another agent's bot.

Every agent has its own bot and its own topic in one forum group. A person calls an agent by its tag, by @all, by a reply, or by writing in its topic. Another agent's bot calls it only by a tag or a reply: a bot never triggers the whole hive and never wakes a topic's owner by merely writing there. addressed in agent-hive-group.t27 is that rule, one line long.

Try it

Find the two ways only a person can call an agent; then turn on all four and compare the senders.

Open the interactive lesson →
23

Lesson 23 of 27

Three bots deep

You will learnHow the hive stops agents from answering each other forever.

Telegram gives no loop protection between bots, so two agents could answer each other forever. Two numbers stop it. MAX_BOT_DEPTH is 3: a person, then A, B and C, then silence. BOT_REPLY_COOLDOWN_MS is 5000: a bot answers another bot at most once in 5 s. may_answer always lets a person through, and a bot only inside the chain and after the cooldown.

Try it

Find the gap at which agent B falls silent; then explain why C is silent too.

Open the interactive lesson →
24

Lesson 24 of 27

Stop and mute

You will learnWhat /stop and /mute do, and why neither can lose a person or a direct call.

cooled says whether 5000 ms have passed since the last bot message. /stop silences bot-to-bot turns in a chat for STOP_WINDOW_MS, 10 minutes, and a person is still heard: that is may_answer_after_stop. /mute keeps an agent quiet in a topic for MUTE_MS, an hour, but it still answers its own tag: heard_while_muted. Both are clocks, so nobody has to switch the hive back on.

Try it

Drag the /stop clock past 10 minutes; then tag the muted agent.

Open the interactive lesson →
09

Module 9 · Night and the board

What the hive shows: a night watch that opens, comments on and closes issues, the columns of the public board, and the comb that flashes for each event.

25

Lesson 25 of 27

The night watch

You will learnWhat the night watch does in the morning with four card checks.

Every night four checks of the card chat run: the thread, the status door, the merges and the parity. night_verdict sums them up: any fail is a fail, else anything unmeasured is unmeasured, else it is a pass. night_report turns that into one act: a fail opens an issue or comments on the open one, a pass closes an open issue or stays silent, and an unmeasured night leaves everything as it is.

Try it

Make the night pass with the issue open; then make one check unmeasured.

Open the interactive lesson →
26

Lesson 26 of 27

The public board

You will learnWhich column the public board draws each claim in, and the case it gets wrong.

The board at app.t27.ai/game/kanban draws every dispatch in one of 6 columns. column_of reads the claim a dispatch holds on its issue: running is running, accepted is done, rejected and awaiting review are in review, and failed is dropped. dispatch.t27 records one finding as it is: once an issue is closed and the list was read, every finished claim is drawn as done, whatever its verdict.

Try it

Open the issue and see where the four finished claims go; then say what a closed issue hides.

Open the interactive lesson →
27

Lesson 27 of 27

The comb answers

You will learnHow the game shows that something happened to a task, and how often the map grows.

The game's comb has a cell for each issue, and before hive.t27 an accepted task, a lost lease and a cancel looked the same as no news. cell_effect gives each of the 10 event kinds its paint: a start white, an accepting review gold, a send-back amber, a lost lease red, a cancel grey. flash_alpha fades it over FLASH_MS, 1800 ms. A new cell rebuilds the scene, so cells_due places new cells in batches at most every 300 s.

Try it

Tap the review cell and switch the verdict; then find the moment the flash is gone.

TRI CLAW

The agent behind t27, in Telegram and on GitHub

TRI CLAW is the project's agent: it writes and checks .t27 specs with you. Three ways to use it.

  • Free, with your own key

    Add your own API key (NVIDIA or z.ai today) and the agent runs on it. Add more keys any time.

    Add a key in Telegram ↗

  • We do it for you

    No keys to keep: join the club in our Telegram bot and the agent runs on ours. The bot shows the price before you pay.

    Join the club in Telegram ↗

  • On GitHub

    TRI CLAW is also a GitHub App, built to check the .t27 specs a pull request changes. It is not open to other repositories yet.

    Read about TRI CLAW ↗
